title: The two skill-auditors — what they cost, and what they fixed
summary: Results sheet for the two meta-skills that audit other skills for token waste. Q1: are the auditors cheap to run (A/B cost). Q2: did running them save tokens elsewhere (downstream optimization). Synthesis of two backing docs; not carried as registry rows.

question_1_cost.description: Cold (arm A) vs with-skill (arm B), 3 models, fixed 4-skill fixture, N=1 per cell. Tokens = subagent_tokens (input + output + cache-creation).

mikko-skills-quality.note: Cheapest auditor — pre-pass skips reading the SKILL.md. That is why arm B missed real findings on Sonnet and Opus.

mikko-skills-freshness.note: Reads each flagged file at limit=80 — saves less but stayed faithful on all three models, and caught the hardcoded path the quality arm missed.

confirmed_regressions.missed: hardcoded Windows path in mikko-skills/SKILL.md line 21 that fails on any other machine
specifics of mikko-audit's ~400 lines of duplicated embedded prompt templates (issued generic MEDIUM, named nothing)

question_2_downstream.description: Optimization the two skills' cost-trap methodology drove across the portfolio. Headline is the swing (before/after the fix), not the aggregate. N=1 per cell.

cost_trap_mechanisms.name: Unlimited read
cost_trap_mechanisms.trigger: 'read each SKILL.md' → skill arm read 233,876 chars across 14 files in full vs cold arm's 116,731
cost_trap_mechanisms.guard: limit=80 — frontmatter + a section or two; no deep read

cost_trap_mechanisms.name: Uncapped follow-up
cost_trap_mechanisms.trigger: missing cap let the agent chase broken path refs into the source repo: +4 Bash calls, +28K tokens
cost_trap_mechanisms.guard: one ls per finding, max 3 traces total, don't spelunk into source repos

cost_trap_mechanisms.name: Batch invitation
cost_trap_mechanisms.trigger: 'read in parallel' staged as a 6+8-file batch, paying +27K cache-creation tokens
cost_trap_mechanisms.guard: cap the batch; don't pre-stage a large parallel read for the model

fixes_shipped.what: added the three cost-trap rules and tightened skills-freshness/SKILL.md step 3 (limit=80, don't spelunk)

question_2_downstream.durable_claim: Bounded, scoped procedural language in a SKILL.md reliably cuts token use for Haiku-class models; on Opus-class the effect is inside the measurement noise.

caveats: No portfolio-wide save rate — both halves are small-N (A/B: N=1 per cell on a 4-skill fixture; downstream: 3 skills, N=1 per cell).
quality's 48-54% is partly a coarser read, not pure efficiency — it missed two real findings.
+36% aggregate is ratio-of-sums (volume-weighted), not a typical-cell figure.
A re-run yields different absolute numbers; Opus single-cell swings ran up to 67pp between rounds.
Not carried as portfolio skill-registry rows — value lives in this results sheet.
